excerpt: How project management works in schools, colleges and universities: academic-calendar constraints, the life cycle, roles, delivery approaches, 2026-27 compliance rules, KPIs and a worked backward schedule for a VLE replacement.
learning_objectives: Explain how education projects differ from projects in other sectors
Plan backwards from a term start date and include governance meetings as constraints
Calculate total float under alternative approval dates and decide on contingency
Check whether a training window has enough capacity
Choose a delivery approach by type of education project
Identify accessibility, data protection and safeguarding requirements to plan for in the UK and US

formulas.formula: Latest start = latest finish - duration (backward pass)
formulas.inputs: go-live Mon 6 Sep 2027; staff last day Fri 16 Jul 2027; migration 6 wk; training 4 wk; pilot 6 wk ending Fri 28 May 2027; configuration 8 wk; contract/onboarding 3 wk
formulas.result: Migration LS Mon 7 Jun; training LS Mon 21 Jun; pilot LS Mon 19 Apr; configuration LS Mon 22 Feb (LF Fri 16 Apr); contract LS Mon 1 Feb 2027 (LF Fri 19 Feb)

formulas.formula: Total float = latest start - earliest realistic start
formulas.inputs: A: approval 16 Dec 2026, work from Mon 4 Jan 2027, config ES Mon 25 Jan; B: approval 17 Mar 2027, work from Mon 22 Mar, config ES Mon 12 Apr
formulas.result: A +4 weeks; B -7 weeks; swing 11 weeks; gap between meetings 13 weeks; paper deadline (10 working days before 16 Dec) Wed 2 Dec 2026

formulas.formula: Sessions needed = ceil(staff / (room capacity x attendance rate))
formulas.variables: staff (people), room capacity (people per session), attendance rate (proportion)

formulas.formula: Sessions available = weeks x days per week x sessions per day x trainers
